narr: A few damaging wind events and an isolated tornado occurred across western Kentucky during the late night/early morning hours. Instability was meager, but very strong wind shear contributed to an environment favorable for a few severe storms. The storms occurred in the warm sector of a surface low centered over northeast Kansas. The storms were far removed from the primary surface fronts, but a 500 mb shortwave rotating northeast toward the lower and mid-Mississippi Valley provided strong forcing for storms. The storms were mainly in bands with embedded weak mesovortices. The multiple bands of storms produced locally heavy rainfall that caused pockets of flash flooding, mainly southeast of a line from Murray to Madisonville. The heavy rain pushed the Green River slightly above flood stage.
ev: Fairly widespread flooding of low-lying roads occurred in the county, several of which were closed. Rainfall amounts of 2 to 5 inches were reported. The highest 24-hour rainfall report in the county was 4.98 inches from the fire weather station at Golden Pond in the Land Between The Lakes area.

Water was over several county secondary roads throughout the county. Rainfall amounts of 2 to 5 inches were reported. The highest 24-hour rainfall report in the county was 4.38 inches just north of Crofton, from a co-op observer.

Flooding was reported in low-lying areas of the county. A pickup truck was stalled in the floodwaters. A culvert was washed out on a secondary road about four miles east-southeast of Murray. Significant flooding was reported on Kentucky Route 783, near the community of Wiswell. Rainfall amounts of 2 to over 5 inches were reported. The highest 24-hour rainfall report in the county was 5.20 inches on the southeast side of Murray.

Significant flash flooding was reported. A few water rescues were conducted. Water was in a few residences. Numerous roads were closed due to flooding throughout the county. The state highways that were closed were Kentucky 181, Kentucky 2590, and Kentucky 2533. Rainfall amounts of 2 to 5 inches were reported. The highest 24-hour rainfall report in the county was 4.98 inches from a Cocorahs observer near Bancroft.
